title: The spectral algebra norm without a complete base field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, and let $E/k$ be an algebraic field extension: every element is a root of a nonzero polynomial over $k$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For $z\in E$ let $p_z(Z)=Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^r a_iZ^{r-i}$ be its monic polynomial of least positive degree vanishing at $z$. Define $s_{E/k}(z)=\max_{1\le i\le r}|a_i|^{1/i}$. Then $s_{E/k}$ is a nonarchimedean $k$-algebra norm: it vanishes exactly at zero, $s_{E/k}(1)=1$, $s_{E/k}(-z)=s_{E/k}(z)$, $s_{E/k}(z+w)\le\max(s_{E/k}(z),s_{E/k}(w))$, $s_{E/k}(zw)\le s_{E/k}(z)s_{E/k}(w)$, and $s_{E/k}(az)=|a|s_{E/k}(z)$ for $a\in k$. No completeness or separability assumption is made. This is Mathlib's $\operatorname{spectralNorm}_k(z)$.
